item.title: Re: How can I get involved in research as a doctor?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The recent BMJ article, “How can I get involved in research as a doctor?”, addresses a question central to modern medical practice. The word doctor derives from the Latin docere, to teach, and reflects a professional obligation not only to treat, but to advance knowledge for the benefit of patients. item.title: Re: Why covid-19 is “a vascular disease masquerading as a respiratory one”
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor While it is encouraging to see recognition that covid-19 is a vascular disease as much as a respiratory condition, there are two fundamental misconceptions presented in this article. Firstly, the article states that “the best preventive measure is vaccination”. This is fundamentally incorrect. item.title: Tattoo inks as a long-term exposure and why primary care should care
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The BMJ report on toxic metals and carcinogens detected in tattoo inks sold in Australia is a useful reminder that tattooing is not only a cultural practice but also a long-term route of chemical exposure, with regulation lagging behind popularity (1). item.title: Re: Scrutiny of the assisted dying bill is vital but obstruction in the House of Lords could mean it never becomes law
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor I have practised medicine for many years and formerly chaired the Ethics Committee of the Royal College of Anaesthetists. Both lead me to share the authors’ concerns regarding the way in which this legislation is heading. Fundamentally, to block this Bill would let down the very many terminally ill people who would benefit so greatly from the choice it would provide. item.title: Re: Scarlett McNally: Shared decision making requires striking the right balance
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor While I share Scarlett McNally's vision for better communication with patients in the consent process and her concern that a significant number of patients regret having an operation, I am disappointed with her use of the term "shared" decision making. item.title: The House of Lords do not obstruct - they adjudicate.
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The Lords are admirably suited to study the Assisted Dying Bill given their stature, age and wisdom. They are closer to the reality than those in The Commons. This is their hour since it is a momentous change in medical practice, has profound ethical and cultural implications and directly assaults the most vulnerable in society. item.title: Prebunking may protect trust better than constant debunking in routine patient communication
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Morgan’s mermaid (1) is a helpful methafor for clinicians because it shifts attention from the content of a falsehood to the craft that makes it persuasive.
